lessons.title: Career paths
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Mia talk about work paths and future plans at a desk in the office.

items.example: Mia wants a long career as an engineer.
items.note: Use ‘career’ when you talk about the work a person does for many years.

items.example: Ben worked well and got a promotion last month.
items.note: Say ‘a promotion’ when someone gets a better, higher job at work.

items.example: She asked for a raise after two years at the bank.
items.note: Say ‘a raise’ when a worker gets more money for their job.

items.example: My grandfather is going to retire next year.
items.note: Use ‘retire’ when an older worker stops working after a long career.

items.example: Sam decided to resign and look for a new job.
items.note: Use ‘resign’ when a worker chooses to leave their job.

items.example: Ana works full-time at the hospital.
items.note: Use ‘full-time’ for a job that takes all five work days each week.

practice.prompt: Mia plans her work life for the next twenty years. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: A career is the work someone does over many years.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: Leo got a promotion at work.
practice.answer: Leo got a promotion at work.
options: Leo got a promotion at work.
Leo got a postcard at work.
Leo got a plaster at work.
practice.explanation: A promotion means moving up to a better job.

practice.prompt: Match each work word or phrase with its meaning.

pairs.right: stop working when you are old

practice.explanation: A raise brings more money, retire is stopping work at an older age, and resign is leaving a job.

practice.prompt: Zara works from Monday to Friday every week. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Zara has a ___ job.
practice.explanation: Full-time means working the whole week, not just a few hours.

practice.prompt: Build a sentence about getting more money at work.
practice.explanation: Say 'got a raise' when your pay goes up.

practice.prompt: Tom wants to leave his old job and study. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Tom is going to ___ next month.
practice.explanation: Tom is young and leaving his job by choice, so he is going to resign.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: My grandfather is going to retire after a long career.
practice.answer: My grandfather is going to retire after a long career.
practice.explanation: People retire at the end of a long career.

story.hook: Why is Omar having a small party in the office?

image.describe: A bright office room with desks and computers: Smarty the black cat and Mia talk with Omar, an older gray cat holding a cup of tea and smiling.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Good morning, Mia! Why is Omar so happy in the office?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: He is going to retire next Friday after a long career here.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Wow! He worked full-time for forty years.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Yes, I loved my profession, and my employer was always kind.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Did you ever want to resign, Omar?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Never! Every co-worker helped me, and I got a promotion and a raise.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: What a great career! We will miss you at work.

questions.prompt: What is Omar going to do next Friday?
questions.explanation: Mia says Omar is going to retire next Friday.

questions.prompt: How did Omar work for forty years?
questions.explanation: Smarty says Omar worked full-time for forty years.

questions.prompt: What did Omar get during his career?
questions.explanation: Omar says he got a promotion and a raise.

mission.setup: Smarty asks you about your dream work path. Answer in your own words.

turns.smarty: Hello! Do you want a full-time job or a part-time job?
accept: ^i would like a (?:full time|part time) job$
turns.hint: Say if you want a full-time job or a part-time job.

turns.smarty: Nice! What do you want in your career, a promotion or a raise?
accept: ^i want a promotion and a raise$
turns.example: I want a promotion and a raise.
turns.hint: Tell Smarty you want a promotion, a raise, or both.

turns.smarty: If you do not like a job, will you stay or resign?
turns.hint: Say 'I will resign' or 'I will stay'.

exposure.gloss: a room or building where people work at desks
a type of job that needs special training
money paid to a worker each week or month
a person you work with
the person or group you work for

lessons.title: Skills
lessons.scenario: Smarty helps Sam and Lily list their best work skills.

items.example: Good communication skills help you speak clearly at work.
items.note: Use ‘communication skills’ when someone is good at speaking, listening, and sharing ideas.

items.example: I like to work in a team with friendly friends.
items.note: Say ‘work in a team’ when you do a job together with other workers.

items.example: A chef can work fast under pressure.
items.note: Say ‘under pressure’ when you must work quickly with very little time.

items.example: Lily is in charge of the new shop.
items.note: Use ‘be in charge of’ when you are the main person responsible for something.

items.example: When there is a problem, Ben likes to take the lead.
items.note: Say ‘take the lead’ when you step forward first to guide others.

items.example: An engineer needs strong attention to detail.
items.note: Use ‘attention to detail’ when someone checks small things carefully so there are no mistakes.

practice.prompt: Ana listens well and explains ideas clearly. What does she have?
practice.explanation: Speaking and listening well are communication skills.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I am good at working in a team.
practice.answer: I am good at working in a team.
options: I am good at working in a team.
I am good at working in a train.
I am good at cooking in a kitchen.
practice.explanation: Working in a team means working together with others.

practice.prompt: Match each skill phrase with what it means.

pairs.right: working well when time is short
be the main worker for a job

practice.explanation: Under pressure is about short time, in charge of is about responsibility, and attention to detail is checking carefully.

practice.prompt: Nobody knows what to do first, so Sam decides to guide the group. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Sam is going to ___.
practice.explanation: Take the lead means going first and guiding the group.

practice.prompt: Build a sentence saying Mia runs the team.
practice.answer: Mia is in charge of the team.
practice.explanation: Use 'is in charge of' to show who leads the team.

practice.prompt: Zara checks every number twice so there is no mistake. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Zara has great ___.
practice.explanation: Checking small facts carefully shows attention to detail.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: I can work well under pressure and take the lead.
practice.answer: I can work well under pressure and take the lead.
practice.explanation: Great job combining two strong work skills!

story.hook: Who is in charge of the big Friday dinner at the restaurant?

image.describe: A busy restaurant kitchen: Sam the orange cat wears a white chef hat and directs Lily and Leo while Smarty the black cat watches from a doorway.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hello, Sam! The restaurant is full tonight.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Yes, Smarty! I am in charge of the kitchen tonight.

lines.speaker: Lily
lines.text: Sam is a great leader. He stays calm under pressure.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Thanks, Lily! We work in a team, and everyone is efficient and flexible.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: I check every plate with attention to detail.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: You all have amazing communication skills too!

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: When we get a promotion, we will celebrate together.

questions.prompt: Who is in charge of the kitchen?
questions.explanation: Sam says: I am in charge of the kitchen tonight.

questions.prompt: How does Sam work when the restaurant is full?
questions.explanation: Lily says Sam stays calm under pressure.

questions.prompt: How does Leo check every plate?
questions.explanation: Leo says he checks every plate with attention to detail.

mission.setup: Smarty is helping you describe your skills for a career. Answer in your own words.

turns.smarty: Do you like to work in a team?
accept: ^yes(?: i do)?(?: i like to work in a team)?$
^i like to work in a team$
turns.example: Yes, I like to work in a team.
turns.hint: Say Yes or No, or say 'I like to work in a team'.

turns.smarty: Can you work under pressure?
accept: ^yes(?: i can)?(?: i can work under pressure)?$
turns.example: Yes, I can work under pressure.
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, I can' or 'No, I cannot'.

turns.smarty: Tell me one skill you have: communication skills or attention to detail?
turns.hint: Say 'I have communication skills' or 'I have attention to detail'.

exposure.gloss: a person who guides a group or team
able to plan work neatly and well
working well without wasting time
able to change plans easily when needed

lessons.title: The CV
lessons.scenario: Ana prepares her CV and cover letter with Smarty to apply for a job.

items.example: Zara has a job interview at ten o'clock tomorrow.
items.note: Say ‘job interview’ for the meeting where an employer asks if you are right for a job.

items.example: Write your school exams and qualifications on your CV.
items.note: Use ‘qualifications’ for the exams, certificates, or training you have passed.

items.example: Ben has two years of work experience in a shop.
items.note: Say ‘work experience’ for the jobs you have already done in the past.

items.example: My old teacher gave me good references.
items.note: Use ‘references’ for people who know your work and can say good things about you.

items.example: Send a cover letter with your CV when you apply for a job.
items.note: Say ‘a cover letter’ for the short letter you send with your CV to explain why you want the job.

items.example: You have great skills, so you should go for the job!
items.note: Say ‘go for the job’ to encourage someone to apply and try to get a job.

practice.prompt: You passed your exams and finished training. What do you write on your CV?
practice.explanation: Exams and training you passed are your qualifications.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I wrote a cover letter for the bank.
practice.answer: I wrote a cover letter for the bank.
options: I wrote a cover letter for the bank.
I wrote a postcard from the park.
I bought a notebook at the shop.
practice.explanation: You write a cover letter to send with your CV.

practice.prompt: Match each CV item with its description.

pairs.right: someone who speaks well of you
a meeting to get a new job

practice.explanation: Work experience is past jobs, references are people who recommend you, and a job interview is the meeting.

practice.prompt: Mia sees a great job at the library. Encourage her to apply.
practice.text: You have the right skills, so ___!
practice.explanation: Say 'go for the job' when someone should try to get a job.

practice.prompt: Build a sentence about past jobs on a CV.
practice.answer: I have work experience in a café.
practice.explanation: Put 'work experience' after 'have' to talk about past jobs.

practice.prompt: The employer wants to call two people who worked with you. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I added two ___ to my CV.
practice.explanation: References are people an employer can contact about your work.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: I sent a cover letter and got a job interview.
practice.answer: I sent a cover letter and got a job interview.
practice.explanation: Sending a strong cover letter helps you get a job interview.

story.hook: Does Ana decide to apply for the museum vacancy before the deadline date?

image.describe: Ana the tabby cat sits at a wooden table with a laptop and papers, showing her CV to Smarty the black cat.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Smarty, look at this vacancy at the history museum.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: You love history, Ana! You should go for the job.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Write about your communication skills in a cover letter.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Good idea! My history teacher can be one of my references.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Send your application before the deadline date tomorrow!

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Thanks, Smarty! I hope I get a job interview as a candidate.

questions.prompt: What does Smarty tell Ana to do about the museum job?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: You should go for the job.

questions.prompt: Where should Ana write about her communication skills?
questions.explanation: Smarty tells Ana to write about her communication skills in a cover letter.

questions.prompt: Who can be one of Ana's references?
questions.explanation: Ana says her history teacher can be one of her references.

mission.setup: Smarty is checking your CV before you apply for a job. Answer in your own words.

turns.smarty: Did you write your qualifications and work experience on your CV?
accept: ^i wrote my qualifications and work experience$
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, I did' or tell Smarty what you wrote.

turns.smarty: Did you also write a cover letter?
accept: ^yes(?: i did)?(?: i wrote a cover letter)?$
turns.example: Yes, I wrote a cover letter.
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, I wrote a cover letter' or 'No, I did not'.

turns.smarty: Are you ready to go for the job and get a job interview?
accept: ^i am ready to go for the job$
turns.example: I am ready to go for the job.
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, I am' or 'Yes, I am ready to go for the job'.

an open job that needs a worker
a person trying to get a job

lessons.title: Review
lessons.scenario: Smarty quizzes Ben and Zara on career paths, skills, and writing a CV.

practice.prompt: Match the career words with their meanings.

pairs.right: a letter sent with your CV

practice.explanation: A promotion is a higher job, a raise is higher pay, and a cover letter goes with your CV.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: She has strong attention to detail and communication skills.
practice.answer: She has strong attention to detail and communication skills.
options: She has strong attention to detail and communication skills.
She has a strong back and a fast bicycle.
She has two qualifications and three references.
practice.explanation: Attention to detail and communication skills are key skills on a CV.

practice.prompt: Ben checks small numbers carefully and guides the group. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Ben is ready to ___ on the new project.
practice.explanation: Take the lead means stepping forward to guide the team.

practice.prompt: Build a sentence about preparing for a job.
practice.answer: Show your qualifications and references clearly.
practice.explanation: Both qualifications and references belong on a strong CV.

practice.prompt: Zara works five full days a week and is the main worker for her team. Which two phrases describe her?
practice.explanation: Working five days a week is full-time, and leading a team means being in charge of it.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: I have work experience, so I will go for the job.
practice.answer: I have work experience, so I will go for the job.
practice.explanation: Good work experience gives you confidence to go for the job.

story.hook: How does Zara get ready for her big job interview tomorrow?

image.describe: A cozy study corner with a desk and lamp: Smarty the black cat reviews a folder with Zara the spotted cat and Ben the brown cat.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Zara, you have a job interview tomorrow! Are you ready?

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: Yes! I packed my CV, my cover letter, and my references.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Tell them about your work experience and qualifications.

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: I will also say I work in a team and stay calm under pressure.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Do not forget you were in charge of the school library last year!

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: True! If I get this full-time job, it will start a great career.

questions.prompt: What does Zara have tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Smarty says Zara has a job interview tomorrow.

questions.prompt: What was Zara in charge of last year?
questions.explanation: Smarty reminds Zara she was in charge of the school library.

questions.prompt: What did Zara pack with her CV?
questions.explanation: Zara packed her CV, cover letter, and references.

mission.setup: Smarty does a quick review with you before your job interview. Answer in your own words.

turns.smarty: What is one skill you will talk about in your job interview?
accept: ^i can (?:work in a team|take the lead|work under pressure)$
turns.example: I can work in a team.
turns.hint: Name a skill like 'work in a team', 'communication skills', or 'attention to detail'.

turns.smarty: Did you bring your CV, cover letter, and references?
accept: ^i have my cv cover letter and references$
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, I did'.

lessons.title: Interview
lessons.scenario: Smarty practises common job interview questions with Tom in the office.

items.example: The manager smiled and said, Tell me about yourself.
items.note: Interviewers start with ‘Tell me about yourself’ to hear a short story about your skills and background.

items.example: My strengths are communication skills and working in a team.
items.note: Say ‘my strengths’ when you talk about the things you do best at work.

items.example: One of my weaknesses is that I sometimes work too late.
items.note: Say ‘my weaknesses’ for areas where you are still learning and getting better.

items.example: Why do you want to work for our hospital?
items.note: Use ‘Why do you want…?’ to ask about a person's reason for choosing a job.

items.example: I am available from Monday next week.
items.note: Say ‘I am available from…’ to tell an employer the first day you can start working.

items.example: Every new worker starts with a trial period of one month.
items.note: Say ‘a trial period’ for the short test time at the start of a new job.

practice.prompt: You want to talk about the skills you do best. Which phrase do you use?
practice.explanation: Your strengths are your best skills and talents.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: Tell me about yourself and your work experience.
practice.answer: Tell me about yourself and your work experience.
options: Tell me about yourself and your work experience.
Tell me about your favourite dessert.
Tell me about your last weekend.
practice.explanation: Interviewers ask 'Tell me about yourself' at the start of an interview.

practice.prompt: Match the interview phrases with their meanings.

pairs.right: things I am still getting better at
the day I can start work
a short test time in a new job

practice.explanation: Weaknesses are areas to improve, available from tells your start date, and a trial period is a test start.

practice.prompt: The interviewer asks your reason for applying. Complete the question.
practice.text: ___ this job?
practice.explanation: Use 'Why do you want' to ask someone's reason.

practice.prompt: Build a sentence telling the employer you can start in June.
practice.explanation: Say 'I am available from' followed by the day or month you can start.

practice.prompt: The first two weeks let both you and the employer test the job. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: We start with ___ of two weeks.
practice.explanation: A trial period is a short test time at the beginning of a job.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: My strengths are attention to detail and working in a team.
practice.answer: My strengths are attention to detail and working in a team.
practice.explanation: Naming clear strengths makes a great impression in an interview.

story.hook: How does Tom handle his first real job interview with Omar?

image.describe: An office room with two chairs across a tidy desk: Omar the older gray cat interviews Tom the young orange cat while Smarty the black cat peeks from behind a plant.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Good morning, Tom. Thank you for the handshake. Tell me about yourself.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Good morning! I am a quick learner with strong communication skills.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Why do you want this full-time job?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I want a career where I can work in a team and help customers.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: What are your strengths and your weaknesses?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: My strengths are attention to detail. One of my weaknesses is a nervous smile at first, so I practise hard!

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: That makes a great impression. There is a trial period of one month. When can you start?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I am available from next Monday!

questions.prompt: What are Tom's strengths?
questions.explanation: Tom says: My strengths are attention to detail.

questions.prompt: How long is the trial period?
questions.explanation: Omar says there is a trial period of one month.

questions.prompt: When is Tom available from?
questions.explanation: Tom says: I am available from next Monday.

mission.setup: Smarty is the interviewer today! Answer his interview questions in your own words.

turns.smarty: Welcome to the job interview! Tell me about yourself.
accept: ^my name is [a-z]+(?: and i am a student)?$
^i am good at working in a team$
turns.hint: Say a short sentence about yourself, like 'I am a student' or 'I am a quick learner'.

turns.smarty: What are your strengths?
accept: ^my strengths are (?:communication skills|attention to detail|working in a team)$
^my strength is (?:communication skills|attention to detail|working in a team)$
turns.hint: Start with 'My strengths are...' and name a skill.

turns.smarty: When can you start the trial period?
turns.hint: Say 'I am available from...' and a day or week.

exposure.gloss: the person who asks questions in a job interview
a small smile when you feel a bit worried
holding and shaking hands to say hello
the feeling or opinion someone gets about you

lessons.title: If I were you
lessons.scenario: Mia and Sam imagine dream jobs and discuss work choices with Smarty.

items.example: If I had more time, I would learn a new language.
items.note: Use ‘If I had…’ with the past form to imagine a situation that is not real right now.

items.example: If I were you, I would go for the job.
items.note: Say ‘If I were you, I would…’ to give friendly advice by imagining yourself in someone else's shoes.

items.example: If I got a promotion, I would be very happy.
items.note: Use ‘I would’ plus a base verb for the imaginary result in a second conditional sentence.

items.example: I wish I could speak four languages at work.
items.note: Say ‘I wish I could…’ when you want to do something that is not possible right now.

items.example: What would you do if you got two job offers?
items.note: Ask ‘What would you do if…?’ to find out someone's choice in an imaginary situation.

items.example: I would rather work in a team than work alone.
items.note: Say ‘I would rather…’ to tell which choice you prefer.

grammar.title: Second conditional: If + past, would + verb
grammar.explanation: Use the second conditional for imaginary situations or advice. Put a past verb after 'if' (including 'If I were you'), and use 'would' + base verb in the result.
examples: If I were you, I would apply for the job.
If I had more time, I would study art.
What would you do if you won a prize?

practice.prompt: Your friend is unsure about applying for a job. How do you start your advice?
practice.explanation: 'If I were you' is the standard second conditional phrase for giving advice.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: If I had more time, I would practise piano.
practice.answer: If I had more time, I would practise piano.
options: If I had more time, I would practise piano.
If I had more money, I would buy a car.
If it rains, I will take an umbrella.
practice.explanation: Use 'If I had more time, I would...' for an imaginary situation.

practice.prompt: Match the two halves of each second conditional sentence.

pairs.right: I would go for the job.

practice.explanation: Pair the 'if' clause with the 'would' result clause.

practice.prompt: Sam cannot fly a plane right now, but it is his dream. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: ___ be a pilot one day.
practice.explanation: Use 'I wish I could' for something you want to do but cannot do now.

practice.prompt: Build a sentence showing your work preference.
practice.answer: I would rather work in a team.
practice.explanation: 'I would rather' is followed directly by the base verb 'work'.

practice.prompt: Complete the second conditional result after 'If I were you'.
practice.text: If I were you, ___ write a cover letter.
practice.explanation: After 'If I were you', use 'I would' + base verb.

practice.prompt: Say the question aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: What would you do if you got a raise?
practice.answer: What would you do if you got a raise?
practice.explanation: Use 'What would you do if' + past verb to ask about an imaginary event.

story.hook: What dream job would Mia choose if she had the chance?

image.describe: A sunny office break corner with two armchairs: Mia the gray-and-white cat and Sam the orange cat drink tea while Smarty the black cat listens.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Imagine you had any dream job, Mia. What would you do if you had the chance?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I wish I could be an astronaut on a space station!

lines.speaker: Sam

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: If I had more time, I would take a cooking workshop with you.

lines.speaker: Sam

questions.prompt: What does Mia wish she could be?
questions.explanation: Mia says: I wish I could be an astronaut on a space station.

questions.prompt: What would Sam rather be?
questions.explanation: Sam says: I would rather be a chef.

questions.prompt: What advice does Smarty give Sam?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: If I were you, I would take the full-time job.

mission.setup: Smarty asks you about imaginary choices and advice. Answer in your own words.

turns.smarty: What would you do if you got a big raise?
accept: ^i would (?:save up|travel|buy a house|buy a car|help my family)$
^if i got a raise i would (?:save up|travel|help my family)$
turns.hint: Start with 'I would...' and say what you would do.

turns.smarty: Would you rather work in a team or work alone?
accept: ^i would rather work in a team$
turns.example: I would rather work in a team.
turns.hint: Say 'I would rather work in a team' or 'I would rather work alone'.

turns.smarty: I am nervous about my job interview. Give me advice with 'If I were you'.
accept: ^if i were you i would (?:practise|go for the job|stay calm|prepare)$
^if i were you i would not worry$
turns.example: If I were you, I would go for the job.
turns.hint: Start with 'If I were you, I would...'

exposure.gloss: to make a picture in your mind of something
the best job you could ever hope for
picking between two or more things
an opportunity to do something

lessons.title: Good advice
lessons.scenario: Smarty acts as a work mentor and gives helpful advice to Leo.

items.example: You really should check your CV before you send it.
items.note: Say ‘You really should…’ to give strong, friendly advice.

items.example: You ought to arrive early for your job interview.
items.note: Use ‘You ought to…’ as a polite way to say what is the right thing to do.

items.example: Why not try asking your teacher for references?
items.note: Use ‘Why not try…?’ to offer a light, easy suggestion.

items.text: It might be a good idea
items.example: It might be a good idea to write a cover letter.
items.note: Say ‘It might be a good idea to…’ when you want to give soft, polite advice.

items.example: I would suggest practising your strengths before tomorrow.
items.note: Say ‘I would suggest…’ to share a helpful work tip.

items.example: You had better hurry or you will be late for work.
items.note: Use ‘You had better…’ when someone needs to act right now to avoid a problem.

grammar.title: Ways to give advice
grammar.explanation: Use 'should', 'ought to', and 'had better' + base verb for strong advice. Use 'It might be a good idea to' + base verb, or 'Why not try' / 'I would suggest' + -ing verb for softer suggestions.
examples: You really should be on time.
You ought to check the details.
Why not try working in a team?

practice.prompt: Leo's train leaves in five minutes and he is still at home. Which advice fits best?
practice.explanation: 'You had better' gives urgent advice so Leo does not miss his train.
